title: Destiny Converges
next_chapter_hook: The figure that vanished into the void left behind one final words. Chen Ji gripped the secret treasure in his hand tightly, his mind reverberating with clues about his father's death, while the sound of footsteps from afar drew ever closer...

text.content:
The阴风 howled through the depths of the ruins, sending a chill down Chen Ji's back. That laughter still echoed, yet it no longer carried the same eerie quality as before—instead, it bore an inexplicable sense of... nostalgia? His pupils contracted sharply, the knuckles gripping the fragment turning white. A figure emerged slowly from the twisted light and shadow, each step seeming to tread upon the wrinkles of time, carrying the weight of centuries.

The person wore a rotted sect robe that had long since decayed, yet his face was unexpectedly young, save for the profound vicissitudes lurking deep within his eyes—a depth utterly incongruent with his apparent age. When that face was fully revealed, Chen Ji's breath caught abruptly—the eyes, they were identical to his own.

dialogue.content: Who are you? Why... why do your eyes look like mine?

text.content: The mysterious figure did not answer immediately, merely gazing at Chen Ji quietly, his gaze sweeping from brow to chin as if confirming something. Finally, his lips curved slightly upward, revealing a bitter smile: "Centuries have passed... I've finally waited for another who can use the Tianji Record." His voice was hoarse and deep, "I've waited for this day, far too long."

dialogue.content: The third master of the Tianji Record—Chen Wujiu. This name, you should have heard.

text.content:
Chen Wujiu. Chen Ji's heart clenched violently. He had heard this name countless times in the occasional fragments Mo Xiansheng had let slip—it was said to be the person who came closest to completing the Tianji Record a thousand years ago, yet suddenly vanished one day. The genealogical records contained only a few sparse words: 'Lord Wujiu, third master of the Tianji Record, suspected to have perished from Heavenly Dao backlash.'

Suspected to have perished? Chen Ji stared at the person before him, his heart churning like tempestuous waves. If this person truly was Chen Wujiu, then he had lived for over three hundred years—older than the entire history of the Tianqing Sect!

dialogue.content: You're wondering why I'm still alive, aren't you? Heh... this body is merely a borrowed remnant soul. Maintaining existence consumes a thread of the Tianji Record Fragment's origin every single day. I'm nothing but a lingering ghost barely clinging to existence.

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. He noticed tiny specks of light constantly dissipating from the edges of the other's form, as if being slowly scorched by an invisible flame. With each breath, this figure seemed to grow even more translucent.

"You've been waiting for me?" Chen Ji's voice was extremely low. "How did you know I would come here?"

dialogue.content: Because I've been watching. Watching you walk to where you are today, from a废物杂役 to one who stirs the winds and clouds... Lad, you're far more interesting—and more dangerous—than any of your predecessors. The Tianji Record choosing you was no coincidence.

text.content:
Chen Ji said nothing, merely gazing quietly at the other. Mo Xiansheng had told him that every master of the Tianji Record met a grim end—the first was directly erased by the Heavenly Will, the second went mad and committed suicide, and this third one before him had somehow managed to cling to existence as a remnant soul for centuries. They had all tried to resist some indescribable force, and in the end, they all failed.

He suddenly felt his throat go dry: "So what? You've waited here—what is it you want to tell me? To warn me to stop? Or to help me walk toward the so-called 'correct ending'?"

dialogue.content: Correct ending? Hah! Lad, there has never been a correct path in this world. The first master couldn't survive three months under the gaze of the Heavenly Eye. The second lost his mind completely after learning the truth... As for me, heh, I watched my own flesh and blood get devoured inch by inch by the Heavenly Secrets. That taste...

text.content:
Chen Wujiu's voice cut off abruptly, his form trembling violently as more specks of light peeled away from his body. Chen Ji instinctively stepped back half a pace, but the other waved his hand, barely steadying himself.

"I don't have much time left." Chen Wujiu's gaze turned sharp. "The more complete the Tianji Record becomes, the stronger the deadly backlash of fate. What you hold now is merely a fragment—the true disaster hasn't even begun. When it reaches over seventy percent assembled... you'll understand what it means when the Heavenly Dao cannot be reversed."

dialogue.content: But you're different. You still have a chance. This is the last thing I can give you—the【Niming Jade Pendant】. It can shield you from the gaze of the Heavenly Eye at critical moments, up to three times, each time no longer than the duration of a burning incense stick. Use it well, and perhaps it can buy you a few more years.

text.content:
A jade pendant warm and smooth as solidified fat appeared凭空 in Chen Wujiu's palm. The pendant was entirely black, yet it emitted scattered starlight within the darkness, as if it contained an entire universe within. The moment Chen Ji reached out to receive it, a chill rushed straight to his crown, and he seemed to hear countless whispers murmuring by his ear.

"The Heavenly Eye has always been watching." Chen Wujiu's voice seemed to come from very far away. "How much of what you think are fortunate coincidences and meticulous calculations truly belongs to your own will? No one in this world can truly outcalculate the Heavenly Dao—neither you nor I."

choice.prompt: Chen Wujiu's words struck like a heavy hammer. Chen Ji felt the weight of fate pressing down heavily. At this moment, he had to make a choice—whether to accept this ancestor's warning and secret treasure, or maintain vigilance and question everything before him?

choices.description: Chen Wujiu was an Chen family ancestor, and the aura of the jade pendant resonated with the Tianji Record. There was no reason to refuse such kindness. The ancestor's experience might help him avoid detours.
choices.visible_cost: Owe Chen Wujiu a Karmic Debt
choices.risk_hint: This person's appearance was too coincidental, and the obsession of waiting hundreds of years was unsettling.

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, carefully tucking the jade pendant away. No matter what, he had to seize this opportunity. "Many thanks, Ancestor. I have another question—if the Heavenly Eye is watching me, what do you mean by that?"

dialogue.content: Do you think those crises that arrive just at the right moment, those fortuitous opportunities that come just when needed, are mere luck? Lad, the Heavenly Eye has been treating you all as pieces on a chessboard, manipulating you for tens of thousands of years. The Tianji Record is merely the sharpest of its many pieces, and we... are nothing more than ants struggling on its board.

choices.description: This person came too mysteriously. On what basis should I believe he is an Chen family ancestor? Behind centuries of waiting, what ulterior purpose lurks? The karmic因果 of the Tianji Record is too heavy to bear lightly.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain independent judgment, avoid karmic debts
choices.risk_hint: If the other party truly means well, refusal may cost vital assistance

text.content: Chen Ji did not reach out his hand, merely gazing silently at the jade pendant. 'There's something I don't understand, senior. You claim to be the third master, yet the family records suggest you died from heavenly dao backlash. If you truly wish to help me, why did you not appear for hundreds of years, only to appear now?'

dialogue.content: Good! Well said, cautious junior! Chen Wuji laughed instead of getting angry, his eyes revealing a hint of admiration. 'A good question indeed. Yes, I have been waiting—for someone who can truly bear the Heavenly Secrets. If I had appeared recklessly before, it would only make you die faster. Now that you possess three fragments of the record, the Eye of Heavenly Dao already watches you. I dare to show myself now. Believe it or not, but you must accept the jade pendant. It can save your life.'

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the jade pendant in his palm, its black surface reflecting his own blurred silhouette. He suddenly spoke: 'You said the Eye of Heavenly Dao watches me. Then I ask you—is my fate already predetermined?' Chen Wuji fell silent for a moment, his fragmented form trembling slightly: 'Predetermined? No, nothing is truly predetermined. The Eye of Heavenly Dao can see the future, but it only sees the most probable outcome among countless possibilities. As long as your actions are sufficiently unexpected, you can break free from the set trajectory... at least theoretically.'

dialogue.content: One final thing I tell you. Your Tianji Record... was not a fortuitous encounter falling from the heavens. It was deliberately left in this world, and that person—shares your bloodline.

text.content: Chen Ji's heart surged violently. Bloodline connection? What did that mean? Could the first master of the Tianji Record also be from the Chen family? Chen Wuji seemed to see through his confusion, his pale lips forming a meaningful smile: 'Do you think the Tianji Record chose your Chen family for no reason? Heh... This question, I shouldn't tell you now. But time is running out.' He suddenly lowered his voice, 'Your father—he did not die from an accident.'

choice.prompt: The words struck like thunder. Chen Ji's mind flashed with his father's final moments, those murky eyes filled with worry, and those words he never finished speaking. Who? Who killed his father?

choices.description: His father's death is the deepest wound in Chen Ji's heart. If there's a chance to learn the truth, he would pursue it at any cost. Even if larger forces are involved behind this.
choices.risk_hint: If the murderer is connected to the Eye of Heavenly Dao, knowing the truth may bring greater danger

dialogue.content: Who? Tell me! Chen Ji's voice suddenly turned ice-cold, those usually calm eyes burning with suppressed fury. Chen Wuji looked at his expression and sighed: 'Your reaction is identical to mine back then... But this matter cannot be discussed here. The Eye of Heavenly Dao is everywhere, walls have ears. If you wish to know, seek the【Destiny Stele】. There, all cause and effect will be revealed. Remember, the entrance to the Destiny Stele is—'

text.content: Chen Wuji's form suddenly trembled violently, more specks of light peeling away from him. He clutched his chest, a flash of pain crossing his face: 'Time's up... My remnant soul cannot hold on any longer. Lad, remember what I said. There's one more thing to give you—'

dialogue.content: Chen Wuji drew out a yellowed bamboo scroll from his怀中, pressing it into Chen Ji's hand before he dissipated: 'This is the【Tianji Fragments·Interpretation】I spent my life refining. Using it with your existing fragments, you can see more... things that should not be seen. But remember, the more you know, the faster you die. Be careful of that old Ling one—he's more dangerous than you imagine... Also, your sister...'

text.content: Before the words finished, Chen Wuji's form completely turned into countless specks of light, dissipating in the chilling wind. Only his final words still echoed in the ruins, carrying the vicissitudes of hundreds of years and unwillingness. Chen Ji tightly gripped the bamboo scroll and jade pendant in his hand, standing silently in place. After a long while, he slowly spoke, his voice low as an abyss: 'Ancestor... I will find the truth with my own hands.'

result_nodes.description: Chen Ji quickly contained his emotional fluctuations. He knew this was not the time for grief or anger. His father's vengeance, he had recorded it. But surviving was more important for now. Only by living could there be a chance for revenge.
result_nodes.visible_reward: Maintain calm judgment,不会被情绪左右
result_nodes.risk_hint: Chen Wuji's words may have had a second half that was missed

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions. His father died from an accident—this was what he had been told since childhood, and his mother never changed her story until her death. Now being told it was not an accident, he反而 became calmer. Accident or not, investigating would clarify things. There were too many things to sort out: the usage of the Counter-Fate Jade Pendant, the mysteries of the Tianji Fragments, Ling Yuan's threat, and also Chen Nian's whereabouts...

dialogue.content: Just then, a jade slip fluttered down from where Chen Wuji dissipated. On the jade slip were four characters carved clearly:【Bloodline Origin】. Chen Ji bent down to pick it up. The jade slip was warm to the touch, and a stream of information directly flooded into his mind—'To know the Chen family's secrets, first seek the Destiny Stele. The stele is in the Northern Wasteland Forbidden Grounds. The entrance requires the Tianji Fragments as a guide. Your father entered once, brought out one thing, and put back half...'

text.content:
Chen Ji stored all the items into his storage bag and turned to look into the depths of the ruins. The eerie wind still howled, but at this moment his heart was unusually calm. Father, sister, Tianji Record, Chen Wuji... all the clues pointed in the same direction—the Fate Stele in the Northern Wasteland Forbidden Grounds.

He raised his head toward the darkness ahead, a cold and ruthless curve forming at the corner of his mouth: "Whoever killed my father, I will find them." Distant footsteps echoed faintly, as if someone was approaching. Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, his figure flashing as he vanished into the shadows...

result_nodes.description: "Rather than taking the initiative to attack, it's better to wait for the visitor. First observe whether they are friend or foe, then decide the next move. Only caution can ensure survival in chaotic times."
result_nodes.visible_cost: "Passive waiting may cause one to miss the initiative"
result_nodes.risk_hint: "If the visitor is an enemy, one may fall into an encirclement"

text.content: Chen Ji did not leave. Instead, he found a hidden corner and收敛his own aura to the extreme. Moments later, a familiar figure appeared in his field of vision—it was Ling Yuan! That seemingly kind old sect master now had none of his usual gentleness on his face, his eyes gloomy and terrifying, like a venomous snake selecting its prey.

dialogue.content: Ling Yuan surveyed his surroundings, his brow furrowed tightly, muttering to himself: "Impossible... that spiritual fluctuation just now was clearly the residual power of the third master. Could that old geezer not be completely dead? Hmph, even if he's not dead, he should have dissipated by now. That boy Chen Ji should have died inside already."

text.content:
Chen Ji watched all this from the shadows, cold fury churning in his heart. What a kind old sect master he had been, all along just putting on an act. He made a mental note of this debt, then silently retreated through another passage. Ling Yuan, you want me dead? Then I'll let you watch your chess game collapse step by step.

Outside the ruins, dawn was breaking. Chen Ji held the jade pendant and bamboo slip in his arms, his gaze deep and profound as an abyss. No matter how many hardships lay ahead, he would not retreat—for his father, for his sister, for those ancestors toyed with by the heavens. Fate? Hmph, he would defy heaven and change his destiny.

Dawn light pierced through the thin mist, falling on Chen Ji's pale face. He slowly opened his eyes, finding himself lying on a piece of icy cold blue stone. His hand still tightly gripped that Reversing Fate Jade Pendant, as if loosening his grip would cause him to lose something precious.

Last night's ordeal felt like an absurd dream, but the jade pendant in his palm and the bamboo slip in his arms silently told him—it was no dream. He had truly met Chen Wuji, the third master of the Tianji Record, that ancestor who had barely maintained himself as a remnant soul for hundreds of years.

dialogue.content:
My father did not die in an accident... What did these words mean? Chen Ji murmured softly, fury suppressed for too long churning in the depths of his eyes. His father's dim yet deeply worried eyes at his deathbed seemed like just yesterday. But he had never imagined that those eyes held not only fear of death, but also profound worry for the fate of him and his sister.

He abruptly sat up, his gaze sharp as a blade: "Ling Yuan... you'd better pray you have nothing to do with my father's death. Otherwise, I'll let you know what it means when heavenly secrets cannot be revealed—reveal them and you die!"

text.content:
Chen Ji stood up, straightened his clothes, and hid the jade pendant and bamboo slip close to his body. The morning wind brushed past, carrying away some of the gloom, but not the killing intent in his heart. He raised his head to gaze at the distant horizon, where clouds churned as if brewing a storm.

The chessboard of fate had been set, the eyes of heaven gazing down at all beings from the nine heavens, while he was still just an insignificant pawn. But even a pawn has its moment to cross the river—then—never retreat another step!

Just then, a familiar aura drifted over from nearby. Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly—that was Su Qingyao's aura. Why would she appear here? Could what happened in the ruins last night already have been discovered?
